caption:
Vienna's most famous wine region is inside the city limits — and its most famous composer's grave has been empty this whole time. 👀

Comment your guess for which fact surprised you most before you swipe ⬇️

1. The Riesenrad
The Riesenrad opened in Prater park in 1897 and is the oldest Ferris wheel still running anywhere on Earth. It was gutted by fire in 1944 and rebuilt with half its original 30 cabins — then went on to star in The Third Man.

2. St. Stephen's Cathedral
St. Stephen's Cathedral's zigzag roof is covered in 230,000 glazed tiles in ten colors, arranged into a double-headed eagle on one side and Vienna's coat of arms on the other — all visible only from a height.

3. Schönbrunn Palace
In 1762, six-year-old Wolfgang Mozart performed for the imperial family in Schönbrunn's Great Gallery, slipped on the polished floor, and was helped up by young Archduchess Marie Antoinette — he's said to have promised to marry her on the spot.

4. The Spanish Riding School
The Spanish Riding School's white Lipizzaner stallions have trained in the Hofburg's baroque Winter Riding School since 1735 — the last place on Earth still practicing classical haute école dressage in its original, unbroken form.

5. Empress Elisabeth
Empress Elisabeth ("Sisi") kept her waist near 19 inches her entire adult life, wrapping herself in damp cloths and installing personal workout equipment in her Hofburg apartments — extreme even by Habsburg standards.

6. Vienna Central Cemetery
Vienna's Central Cemetery holds a place of honor for Mozart among Beethoven, Schubert, and Strauss — but it's a memorial, not a burial. His actual grave, in a different Vienna cemetery, was unmarked and its exact spot was lost.

7. The vineyards
Over 600 hectares of working vineyards sit inside Vienna's city limits, legally protected from ever becoming anything but vineyard. The blend grown there, Wiener Gemischter Satz, can't legally be made anywhere else.
